title: The Grove Where Roots Still Refuse

features.name: the shed that stayed
features.desc-on-touch: A small structure stands here, weathered but resolute. It refused to be pulled from the earth. The roots beneath it argue back.

features.name: the roots that answer
features.desc-on-touch: Deep networks of root run beneath the grove. They touch each other and say: we will not climb. We will stay. The argument learns it has a voice.

features.name: the forest's counter-proposal
features.desc-on-touch: Trees stand rooted here, making a claim. Not fleeing, not fighting. Simply: this is where we will not leave.

features.name: the boundary stone
features.desc-on-touch: Where demand meets refusal and both choose to stop speaking. The stone marks the place where argument becomes presence instead.

features.name: the shopfront that would not close
features.desc-on-touch: Stacked timber and a counter. A register, a bell on the wall still sounding through roots. Still open to no one. Still refusing the road.

reverie.title: REVERIE — under the shed where trees learn to hold their gro
narr: The truck is packed. Leif holds the key. She stands in the
forest under the old shed, and the roots argue with what she
knows: that the mesh is still half-built. The trees will not move.
She will not move. He says: you could leave. She shakes her head.
The roots will stay. The shed will stand. The forest wins by not

inscription: down is no longer a suggestion, and the roots have learned to say no
